title: My first SC: a week of science and connections in Chicago
description: A photo diary from McCormick Place: AgenticAI4HPC, the Early Career Program, mentoring events, SPIKE, and catching up with NASA Flight Science Lab colleagues.

title: Presenting Recall Is Not Honesty at AgenticAI4HPC’26
description: Presented our work with Kartik Shinde at SC26, examining what makes multi-agent HPC operational analytics trustworthy. Our Trustworthy HPC poster was also on display during the week.

title: SPIKE at SC26: attention through spikes
description: Shared SPIKE at the DOE booth at SC26: spiking attention, scalable neural simulation, and neuromorphic hardware, led by ORNL’s Dr. Prasanna Date.

title: Can an abstract become a quantum experiment?
description: Qatalyst explores how teams of agents reconstruct equations, Qiskit code, and simulated circuits from scientific abstracts.

title: Talk at Oklahoma State University: From Ph.D. to National Lab: A Journey into Research, Innovation, and Impact
description: Gave a talk at Oklahoma State University as an ORNL postdoctoral researcher, sharing my research experiences and discussing national laboratory research careers, interdisciplinary collaboration, and advice for graduate students, including international students. The session ran from 4:00–5:00 PM Eastern Time.

title: ORPA All-Around Excellence Award
description: Recognized by Oak Ridge Postdoctoral Association leadership for contributions to research, publications, presentations, and new-employee support.

title: ORPEX President’s Award
description: Recognized by Oak Ridge Postdoctoral Association leadership for contributions to research, publications, presentations, and new-employee support.

title: Astronomy language models: when does specialization help?
description: New preprint: “Rethinking Domain Specialization for Open-Ended Scientific Reasoning in Astronomy Language Models.”

title: Selected for the URA SPARC Fall 2026 cohort

title: Evaluating scientific hypotheses with model confidence
description: New preprint: “Do LLMs Know a Good Hypothesis When They See One?” The study compares intrinsic model scoring with prompted hypothesis ranking.

title: Tracing mechanisms from graphs to scientific answers
description: New preprint: “Visualizing Graph-to-Answer Mechanism Recovery in Materials-Science Hypothesis Generation.”

title: Interpretable machine learning for antenna design
